deliverables_scope.text: t der Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung gemäß § 21 VgV über die Bereitstellung von Softwarelizenzen (SaaS / On-Premise) sowie damit verbundenen Dienstleistungen (Implementierung, Support, Wartung). Im Rahmen dieser Rahmenvereinbarung behält sich der Auftraggeber vor, während der Vertragslaufzeit von voraussichtlich 36 Monaten Einzelbedarfe durch Abruf zu bestellen. Der konkrete Umfang der abzurufenden Leistungen – insbesondere die Anzahl der Nutzer bzw. Lizenzen – wird zum Zeitpunkt des Vertragsschlusses nicht abschließend festgelegt, sondern ergibt sich aus dem tatsächlichen Bedarf des Auftraggebers. Das in Aussicht genommene Auftragsvolumen wird wie folgt angegeben: Schätzmenge: 400 Nutzer über 36 Monate (entspricht 14.400 Nutzermonten) Höchstmenge: 600 Nutzer über 36 Monate (entspricht 18.000 Nutzermonten) bzw. ein Höchstwert von 250.000,00 € netto Die Rahmenvereinbarung verliert automatisch ihre Wirkung, sobald die Höchstmenge oder der Höchstwert erreicht ist. Die Angabe der Schätzmenge dient ausschließlich der Orientierung der Bieter und begründet keine Abnahmeverpflichtung des Auftraggebers. 2.11. Mitteilung über nicht berücksichtigte Angebote Sofern auf das Angebot kein Zuschlag erfolgen soll, wird dies dem betreffenden Bieter gemäß § 134 des Gesetzes gegen Wettbewer

elt und der genaue Nutzungsumfang noch unklar ist. Zu diesem Zweck wird ein fester Wertungspreis ermittelt und ein Angebotspreisblatt abgefragt. Der Wertungspreis muss auf Basis des Angebotspreisblatts erstellt werden. A. Wertungspreis Aufgrund verschiedenster Kalkulationsmodelle wird zur besseren Vergleichbarkeit der Angebote von den Bietern ein Wertungspreis abgefragt. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case -processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural pr

public health through development of data and knowledge that are translatable, predictive, and timely. The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based m

e approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models. This work is funded by an external NIH grant in collaboration with NCATS through a Complement-ARIE grant award to develop human- based microphysiological systems and test methods that better model human health (in this case, the initial work will focus on liver). 3) Scope: The Contractor shall provide a Fluigent Microencapsulation Platform, in accordance with the obtained vendor quotation. The system shall include the require

formation of three-dimensional (3D) microtissues and organoids. The Contractor shall also provide installation and training for the Fluigent system at the NIEHS facility. Vendor representatives shall perform system setup and provide training to facilitate rapid onboarding and use of the technology. The system will operate independently of NIEHS information technology (IT) systems and will not require NIEHS IT support. The computer and software components are expected to be delivered by the end of September 2026. Full system installation and training are expected to be completed in Fall 2026, subject to vendor engineer scheduling availability. Work shall be performed at NIEHS, Rall Building 101, Laboratories E144–146.
